name: Madison Air

logo.source: investors.madisonair.com site header logo (https://investors.madisonair.com/images/MadisonAir_2026_H_FullColor_RGB.svg); no Wikipedia page

description: Madison Air makes and sells air-quality equipment: custom and semi-custom air handling, precision air and liquid cooling for data centers, industrial fans and heaters, humidity control and energy-recovery products for commercial and industrial buildings (about two-thirds of sales), plus whole-home ventilation, filtration and humidification products sold through professional channels and retailers (about one-third). Customers buy equipment once, mostly through projects, distributors and contractors; about half of 2025 sales came from replacement and upgrade demand and about 10% from aftermarket parts and services. The growth driver is data-center cooling: more than half of Commercial's 2025 organic growth came from it, and Commercial backlog rose to $2.8 billion by 2026-06-30 from $1.2 billion a year earlier. It is controlled by its founder through Madison Industries Holdings (64.7% economic interest and 95.2% of votes at 2026-06-30) and signed an EUR 4.775 billion deal in August 2026 to buy ebm-papst, a German maker of fans and motors.

sub.name: Heating, cooling, elevators, lighting and building controls

hq.note: 444 West Lake Street, Suite 4460 (10-Q cover). Decentralized: material operations also in Canada, Mexico, China, the UK and Europe.

employees.note: 'Over 8,650 employees' (424B4 prospectus filed 2026-04-17; as-of date not given in the sentence read).

businessLines.name: Commercial
businessLines.how: One-time sale of engineered air-handling and cooling systems and fans, priced per project or order and sold through contractors, engineers, distributors and direct to data-center and industrial customers; some aftermarket parts and service after installation.
businessLines.description: Highly engineered air systems for mission-critical and industrial environments. Five platforms: air handling; air and liquid cooling (data centers); air movement and heat; humidity control and dedicated outdoor air systems; energy efficiency enablers. Brands include Nortek Air Solutions, Nortek Data Center Cooling, Big Ass Fans, Addison and Reznor.

operatingProfit.note: Segment Adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP, not operating income); FY2024 $508.4M. Q2 2026: $173.1M vs $156.0M; first half 2026: $334.1M vs $284.4M.

businessLines.name: Residential
businessLines.how: Product sales to HVAC wholesale distributors, builders and retailers, with a recurring replacement-filter and consumables tail (the company says AprilAire filters can bring up to nine times the original air cleaner sale over its life).
businessLines.description: Healthy Air System products for homes: purification (filters, air cleaners), ventilation (bath fans, range hoods), humidification, dehumidification, sensors and controls. Brands include AprilAire, Broan-NuTone and Zephyr.

revenue.note: +39.1% vs $821.2M, mostly the AprilAire acquisition (2025-05-07). Q2 2026: $333.8M vs $287.3M (organic -4.8%); first half 2026: $649.4M vs $484.8M (organic -3.4%).
